method.all_thread_wall_command: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 PYTHONPATH=src py-spy record --format raw --rate 50 --threads --idle --nonblocking --full-filenames -- python3 -m twixt_ai.evaluation.cuda_selfplay_512_cli --output-dir /path/to/scratch/selfplay-wall-out --report /path/to/scratch/wall-report.json --implementation-label post-scheduling-all-thread-wall-profile-nonblocking --worker-concurrency 8 --inference-batch-size 8 --queue-flush-max-wait-seconds 0.002
method.sampling: The 100 Hz --gil profile ranks executable Python paths. The complementary nonblocking 50 Hz all-thread profile includes idle/waiting workers and retains the Python evaluate_batch boundary while its thread is in native inference. Both filter MCTS evidence to ThreadPoolExecutor workers; post-timing validation occurs on MainThread and is excluded.
method.classification: Exclusive deepest-stack/source-line classification. Nested win and legal-move functions take precedence; automatic-link rules are state transitions; direct tuple sorting and GameState._from_canonical are allocation/copy; choose_move lines 371-373 are backup and lines 375-461 are metadata construction.
limitations: Sampling percentages are relative evidence, not exact function timers.
The --gil view ranks executable Python work and intentionally omits native CUDA time and time workers spend waiting for inference or the GIL; it is not used alone for an end-to-end conclusion.
The nonblocking all-thread view accounts thread residence and waits but cannot identify the GIL owner in each sample, so GIL contention is bounded rather than point-estimated.
Profiled wall times are diagnostic; retained unprofiled runs remain the throughput source of truth.

gil_ranking_run.phase_breakdown_limitation: This runner sampler inspects all threads, but its priority classifier labels a worker blocked in NeuralInferenceBatcher.__call__ as cpu_mcts whenever the inference thread is not in evaluate_batch. It is retained as raw corroboration and is not used to quantify CPU execution or GIL wait.

thread_and_gil.interpretation: All eight game workers contributed GIL-held MCTS samples, but sample balance establishes participation rather than contention cost. The complementary all-thread run finds only 25.16 aggregate thread-seconds resident in MCTS after excluding inference-future waits, versus 601.84 thread-seconds explicitly waiting for inference.
thread_and_gil.bound_derivation: After explicit inference waits are excluded, only 25.16 aggregate worker thread-seconds remain resident anywhere in MCTS. Even if every such sample were waiting on a GIL held by another worker, the inference thread, or the main thread, GIL wait and its possible end-to-end impact cannot exceed 25.16 seconds. This is deliberately conservative and includes actual MCTS execution; actual GIL wait may be zero.
thread_and_gil.measurement_boundary: The 27.33 GIL-ranking sample-seconds and 25.16 all-thread resident-seconds come from separate equivalent runs and agree only to sampling/run variation; their difference is not a wait estimate. The evidence does not resolve a positive GIL-wait cost.

conclusion.remaining_end_to_end_bottleneck: The shared synchronous inference path is the largest measured limiter: an average 7.35 of eight game workers wait on inference futures, and evaluate_batch occupies 34.96 sampled seconds (42.70% of wall; 37.845 seconds or 46.22% by its runner timer). Non-waiting MCTS residence is 25.16 aggregate thread-seconds (0.31 worker on average). The earlier near-even runner phase split cannot establish CPU co-dominance because its priority classifier includes inference-future waits under cpu_mcts.
conclusion.ranked_next_target: For the next end-to-end change, target shared inference service/synchronous wait rather than GIL scheduling, selection, or backup. If CPU MCTS work is revisited after inference, expansion/initialization remains its first source-ranked target at 42.04% of executable MCTS samples; expansion plus transition and state-copy work is 66.70%.
